problem: REQ-2's zero-human carve-out for Mode B is scoped narrowly: 'the only permitted human contribution is COMPUTE (a subscription) + a one-time payout identity at install.' REQ-11 separately (and honestly) admits 'phone-gated X/note account creation is NOT yet proven [zero-human]' as a self-create fallback. REQ-15 assumes credentials for a platform simply pre-exist in the install's env ('an install activates only rails whose creds exist') without saying who/what creates the underlying platform ACCOUNT (as opposed to the payout identity). Sprint 2's entire money milestone targets exactly the note rail (verification-architecture.md:57), which REQ-11 itself flags as not-zero-human-provable to create. The spec never states whether creating/verifying the note.com account (distinct from the 'one-time payout identity') is: (a) covered by REQ-2's 'one-time...at install' carve-out (in which case REQ-2 should say so explicitly, since payout identity != platform account), or (b) a separate, undeclared human dependency that sits outside REQ-2's accounting entirely. As written, a reader cannot determine whether the note account for Sprint 2 is allowed to be human-created at install (compliant) or must be proven zero-human-creatable per REQ-11 before Sprint 2 can claim Mode-B compliance (in which case Sprint 2 is currently blocked, since REQ-11 says note creation is unproven).
fix: Extend REQ-2's install-time carve-out to explicitly name 'platform account creation/verification for credential-gated rails' alongside 'payout identity' (both one-time, install-adjacent, human-permitted acts, distinct from the runtime publish loop), OR state explicitly that Sprint 2's note rail requires a human-created account as an accepted install-time exception and is NOT claimed to be zero-human end-to-end until account self-creation is proven.
